reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis relies on THz-TDS to measure electronic relaxation times and separate electronic from lattice contributions, but THz-TDS primarily probes low-frequency vibrational modes and free-carrier response, and it is not established that it can cleanly isolate electronic thermal conductivity in a highly disordered metallic alloy, especially at elevated temperatures where phonon contributions dominate the dielectric response.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear in principle, but the practical feasibility of performing INS and THz-TDS across the full 300–1200 K range on the same sample, and then independently deriving thermal conductivities from these spectra without a validated transport model, is extremely challenging and the falsification criterion is well-defined.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses the core challenge of decoupling lattice and electronic transport, but it proposes a measurement-based calibration rather than a new predictive theoretical framework, and it does not explain how the model would outperform existing DFT-based approaches without relying on the very measurements it seeks to predict.
